decisions.reason: The MMAK concept is central to Doppstadt's announced mobile-modular direction and is backed by a publicly cited customer saving of over 600,000 euros a year, so management has strong reasons to keep it.
The mobile slow-speed shredder has kept its own page across both years and belongs to the firm's core shredding range, which makes it a heavily invested, visible product the firm will persist with.
This MMAK listing carries a named reference customer (Wiese Umwelt Service) and quantified savings, so the public commitment and positive evidence make keeping it very likely.
The slow-speed shredders were launched only in 2024 on their own page, so any weak early results can be put down to temporary market-entry causes, and the product sits in the firm's core business.

The mobile spiral shaft screens are a recent, prominently presented addition to the mobile screening line, and the firm will give them time to justify the investment, even though the earlier trommel screen was dropped.
